diagnosis_explanation:
Your baby was born early. They were born 8 weeks before their due date. This means they are a premature baby.

Your baby had trouble breathing when they were born. This is called respiratory distress syndrome. Their lungs needed extra help to work well.

Your baby was smaller than expected for their age in the womb. This is called intrauterine growth restriction.

Your baby had a low number of platelets in their blood. Platelets help your blood to clot. This condition is called thrombocytopenia.

Your baby had low blood sugar. This is called hypoglycemia. It means their body did not have enough energy.

Your baby's eyes are still developing. This is called retinal immaturity. Their eyes will continue to grow after birth.
medication_rationale:
Mylicon drops:
This medicine is to help your baby's tummy. It can help relieve gas bubbles. Your baby may burp more or seem less fussy. This is a sign the medicine is working. Call your doctor if your baby has trouble breathing or seems to be in pain.

Glycerin Suppositories:
This medicine helps your baby have a bowel movement. It is inserted into the bottom. It makes it easier to poop. Your baby may poop soon after this is used. Call your doctor if your baby has a fever or seems sick.

Reglan:
This medicine helps the muscles in the stomach work better. It helps food move from the stomach to the gut faster. This can help your baby feel more full. You may notice your baby eats less at each feeding. Call your doctor if your baby seems very sleepy or has jerky movements.

NeoSure:
This is a special formula to help your baby grow. It has extra nutrients for premature babies. Your baby will get the nutrients needed to grow strong. This formula is helping your baby gain weight. Call your doctor if your baby has a rash or seems to be having trouble breathing.

Diazoxide:
This medicine helps relax the blood vessels in your baby's body. This can help improve blood flow. Your baby's blood pressure may become lower. This is a sign the medicine is working. Call your doctor if your baby's breathing changes or if your baby seems very weak.

Iron:
This medicine helps your baby make red blood cells. Red blood cells carry oxygen through the body. Your baby may have darker stools. This is a normal sign the iron is working. Call your doctor if your baby has tummy pain or seems very tired.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will feel sleepy and may need to be held often.
- You can eat and drink by mouth.
- Watch for fever over 100.4 degrees Fahrenheit.
- Your goal is to drink well from a bottle or breast.
- You had eye exams. You will get another one later.
- You will get follow-up eye exams after discharge.
- Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.

**Week 2:**
- You may start to feed better this week.
- You can move around gently.
- Continue to watch for fever over 100.4 degrees Fahrenheit.
- Your goal is to finish most of your bottle feedings.
- Call your doctor if you seem very sleepy or hard to wake.

**Week 3:**
- You might seem more alert and active this week.
- You can sit with help for short periods.
- Watch for any new rashes or skin problems.
- Your goal is to have steady weight gain each day.
- Call your doctor if you have trouble keeping food down.

**Week 4:**
- You may start to smile and make more sounds.
- You can enjoy tummy time for longer periods.
- Watch for any changes in your eyes.
- Your goal is to sleep for longer stretches at night.
- Call your doctor if you seem to be having trouble breathing.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Your baby will grow stronger each week.
- Keep up with regular feeding and sleeping times.
- Follow up with your doctor as scheduled.
- Premature babies grow at their own pace.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Breathing stops or slows: Your baby needs help breathing.
- Pale or blue lips or skin: This means low oxygen.
- Not waking up or very sleepy: Your baby may be sick.
- Seizure or body shaking: This is a medical emergency.
- Cannot keep any milk down: Your baby can get dehydrated.
- Vomiting large amounts of green fluid: This can be serious.
- Cold to touch or unable to keep warm: Baby's body is failing.
- Rectal temperature over 100.4 F: This can be a serious infection.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Baby seems sick or listless: Your baby may need care.
- Refusing to feed or taking much less: Baby needs fluids urgently.
- Breathing fast or looks like work: Your baby may struggle to breathe.
- Diaper rash that looks worse: This can become a bad infection.
- Baby has trouble breathing after medicine: Call your doctor first.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Questions about medicine or dose: Your nurse can help you.
- Baby's stool is hard or baby is straining: Try glycerin suppository.
- Mild gas pain that Mylicon does not help: Talk to your doctor.
- Baby's skin looks slightly yellow: This can be normal jaundice.
- Rash that is small and not spreading: Watch for signs of infection.
